Jonas / all — attaching a small sample (mediq_audit_sample.csv) that mirrors what our audit stream currently retains. High level:

- Included event types: auth.login, auth.logout, admin.role_change, model.request_start, model.request_end, billing.usage_summary.
- Per-event metadata: timestamp, user_id (hashed), session_id, request_id, model_id, token_counts, latency_ms, response_status.
- We do not log full request payloads for hosted API by default; only metadata. For Dedicated/Private we can offer request-level capture for POCs with opt-in (privacy and cost implications).
- Redaction: PII fields are hashed; we have a configurable pipeline to drop or redact text fields.

Attachment: mediq_audit_sample.csv

Quick ask: do we want to include an example of a retention policy row (e.g., event_type, default_retention_days, adjustable_by_admin:true/false)? If yes I can add.

Thanks Marcus — sample looks good. A few clarifications on retention:

- Current platform: retention windows are global at product-config level (per deployment) not per-customer. We can support per-account retention only on Dedicated and Private by adding a per-tenant policy table (engineering effort estimated).
- UX: exposing per-account retention requires Admin UI changes + policy enforcement in the ingest pipeline. Estimate: 3 sprints (6 weeks) to implement a minimal per-account retention feature on Dedicated; 2 additional weeks for QA/security review.
- Short-term workaround: we can provide an exported evidence bundle on demand (ad-hoc) with selected event types and a time slice (e.g., last 90 days) as a one-off deliverable for POC. That is lower effort and acceptable for compliance review.

Suggested language for MedIQ: "Redwood currently stores structured audit events (auth/admin/model metadata). For the POC we can deliver an export containing the requested event classes and retention window as a dated evidence bundle. Roadmap work would enable per-tenant retention controls in Dedicated/Private deployments."

I'll add this to the packet if Jonas agrees.

- Grace
Product Manager, Observability

Quick BYOK summary for packet:

- Hosted: no customer-managed keys. We use platform-managed keys and cannot expose key material for hosted customers.
- Dedicated: BYOK possible through a KMS integration (customer supplies key in supported KMS — AWS KMS, Google KMS). Rotation is supported but requires coordination; keys are used to wrap service-level encryption keys.
- Private (on-prem / VPC): full BYOK and HSM options available; customer retains key control.

For the MedIQ POC (they are evaluating us but want short timeline): we can offer a timeboxed Dedicated POC with KMS-backed encryption. Limitations/notes:
- We will not provide key import/export for the POC (no key material transfer).
- We can provide key rotation logs and a KMS audit bundle (kms_options_summary.pdf attached) that shows rotation events and use.
- Implementation effort: platform + infra change to provision a per-tenant KMS binding for the POC (estimate: 2 weeks infra + 1 week integration testing).

If that's acceptable I can sync with Infra to schedule.

- Lauren
Head of Trust & Safety
